newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FNB slides to 14-month low on poor results.
newsitem.headline: FNB slides to 14-month low on poor results.

text.p: A poor set of annual results from South Africa's First National Bank Holdings Ltd (FNB) knocked over five percent off the share's value on Thursday, pushing it to its lowest level in 14 months.
"The results are pushing the price down," one Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) dealer said.
"People are worried about the massive increase in specific provisions as it shows FNB has specific problems, most likely in their Wesbank and FirstPref divisions," the dealer said.
Results released on Wednesday showed FNB's headline earnings up a meagre eight percent to 229.8 cents a share in the year to September 30, well below analysts expectations of a 17 percent rise.
The bottom line was particularly hard hit by a 69 percent surge in bad debts to 665.2 million, with specific provisions growing by a massive 82 percent.
FNB said businesses responsible for the rise, instalment financiers Wesbank and FirstPref, had already tightened their lending entry levels.
Dealers said a general retracement in the JSE's banking and insurance sectors after a recent strong run-up compounded the share's weakness.
"The whole market is also down today, which isn't helping. But the main reason is the results," another trader said.
At 1040 GMT shares had lost 130 cents or 5.2 percent to 23.65 rand, their weakest level since September last year when they traded at 23.50 rand.
